raw_response:
I'm 60 this year, and I've been farming these 15 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. I studied agriculture at university back in the day, so I know the theory, but theory doesn't pick cotton or haul fertilizer bags. It's just me and my wife now—our son works in Shijiazhuang—so labor is the real constraint. That's why I keep only 5 mu in cotton. Any more and we'd drown in the picking. The other 10 mu stays in wheat-maize double crop, which I can manage mostly with machinery and custom hiring for harvest.

The wheat went in last October, second week. I used Jinmai 47, an improved variety I've had good luck with. Base dressing was 50 kg/mu of 15-15-15 compound plus 8 kg urea— that put down about 10 kg N/mu along with the P and K. Now it's March, wheat is greening up, and the stand looks decent. I'm targeting 480 kg/mu. With the soil organic matter around here at about 1.5%, I need roughly 19 kg N/mu total. So this spring I'll topdress in two splits: 10 kg urea per mu at green-up in early March, and another 8 kg urea at jointing if the lower leaves start yellowing. That's the advantage of splitting—you can adjust. I'll irrigate four times: green-up, jointing, flowering, and grain-filling. At about 25 yuan per mu per irrigation, that's 100 yuan/mu just for water, but you can't skip jointing or flowering. I'll spray a fungicide for rust prevention and a herbicide if I see wild oats coming up. My wife and I will handle the spring work, but I'll hire two days of help at harvest to get the wheat out fast.

For maize, I've already bought Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed at 70 yuan/mu. The planting window after wheat harvest is brutal—sometimes only three days before you start losing yield to delayed emergence. I'll rotary till immediately after combining the wheat, then plant and put down 40 kg/mu of compound fertilizer. At the big trumpet stage I'll side-dress 15 kg urea. Two irrigations should be enough if the summer rains cooperate—one at tasseling, one at grain fill. Yield target is 520 kg/mu. Between planting, managing, and harvest, that's about six days of our labor plus one day of hired help for hauling.

Cotton goes in mid-April on the 5 mu. I'll plow and harrow first, then plant with 40 kg/mu compound fertilizer as base. I'll topdress with urea at flowering. Cotton needs more pesticide attention—bollworm is always a threat, and I'll watch for aphids early. I'll irrigate twice, but I'm careful because cotton water use efficiency matters and pumping isn't cheap. The real issue is labor: between planting, management, and picking, my wife and I will put in 25 days, and I'll hire another 8 days of picking labor at 150 yuan per day. That's 1,200 yuan just for hired help on 5 mu. It's why I don't grow more cotton no matter what the price does. I expect about 300 kg/mu of seed cotton.

Total input costs will run about 10,800 yuan this year. That's a big chunk of our cash, but wheat is at 2.4 yuan/kg and maize at 2.2, so the numbers work. Cotton at around 7.5 yuan/kg for seed cotton helps too. At my age, I'd rather apply a bit more fertilizer than risk a bad year—losing 100 kg/mu hurts more than saving 50 yuan on inputs.
